LESSON: PRESENT CONTINUOUS TENSE

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade one
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 6
Topic 6.3: Present continuous tense
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Present continuous tense, part of Strand 6 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade one ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: Why do we use present continuous tense?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Present continuous tense together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Communication and collaboration – Learner’s team work spirit is enhanced as they contribute to group decisions as they retell short stories using the

present continuous tense.

Values:
Unity: Cooperation is enhanced as the learner strives to achieve a common goal as they role play events using the present continuous tense.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Education for Sustainable Development - Environmental Education is enhanced as the learner asks and answers questions about the weather.

Links to other Learning Areas:
The present continuous tense is a key feature in Kiswahili and Indigenous Language Activities.

Suggested learning resource

• Audio, video clip,

• Textbooks in braille and in appropriate font and colour contrast.
